# V1.44 — next micro-scope

V1.44 must remain conditional on the same trigger. The most useful next step
is **not** another cache feature; it is a broader production orchestration
search around the first real rendering/generation vertical slice.

1. trace the first production entry point from entity/component creation toward
   geometry and rendering;
2. identify whether `resolve_component()` is intentionally bypassed or simply
   not wired yet;
3. compare the generic resolution contract with the actual geometry/appearance
   consumers that already exist;
4. determine whether generic resolution is still an active production path or
   an intentionally library-level API;
5. if a real caller appears, map its exact owner/destructor boundary before
   injecting the cache;
6. if no caller appears, record the architectural boundary explicitly and do
   not create a manager;
7. measure the first real vertical-slice lifetime if one exists;
8. only then revisit shared/partitioned ownership and byte budgets;
9. keep `ResolutionFingerprint.cache_identity` as the sole semantic key;
10. repeat single-flight, stale-graph, cross-surface and teardown tests after
    any real integration;
11. preserve the COLOR boundary strictly unless a distinct downstream color
    consumer is independently discovered.

The next implementation is therefore **consumer-driven**, not version-driven:
the appearance of a real production resolver caller is the event that unlocks
runtime cache integration.
